[[Mathematics]] is a broad subject that is commonly divided in many '''areas'''  or '''branches''' that may be defined by [[List of mathematical objects|their objects of study]], by the used methods, or by both. For example, [[analytic number theory]] is a subarea of [[number theory]] devoted to the use of methods of [[mathematical analysis|analysis]] for the study of [[natural number]]s.

This glossary is alphabetically sorted. This hides a large part of the relationships between areas. For the broadest areas of mathematics, see {{slink|Mathematics#Areas of mathematics}}. The [[Mathematics Subject Classification]] is a hierarchical list of areas and subjects of study that has been elaborated by the community of mathematicians. It is used by most publishers for classifying mathematical articles and books.

==A==

{{glossary}}
{{term|[[Ricci calculus|Absolute differential calculus]]}}
{{defn| An older name of {{gli|Ricci calculus}} }}
{{term|[[Absolute geometry]]}}
{{defn| Also called {{gli|neutral geometry}},<ref>{{Citation | author-link=Marvin Greenberg|last=Greenberg|first=Marvin Jay| title=Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometries: Development and History|edition=4th|place=New York|publisher=W. H. Freeman|year=2007|isbn=978-0-7167-9948-1}}</ref> a [[synthetic geometry]] similar to [[Euclidean geometry]] but without the [[parallel postulate]].<ref>{{Citation |title=Foundations of Euclidean and Non-Euclidean Geometry |last=Faber |first=Richard L. |year=1983 |publisher=Marcel Dekker |location=New York|isbn=0-8247-1748-1 }}</ref>}}
{{term|[[Abstract algebra]]}}
{{defn| The part of {{gli|algebra}} devoted to the study of [[algebraic structure]]s in themselves.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Whitehead | first1=C. | title=Guide to Abstract Algebra | edition=2nd | isbn=978-0-333-79447-0 | year=2002 | publisher=Palgrave | location=Houndmills}}</ref> Occasionally named {{gli|modern algebra}} in course titles.}}
{{term|[[Abstract analytic number theory]]}}
{{defn| The study of [[Abstract analytic number theory|arithmetic semigroup]]s as a means to extend notions from [[analytic number theory|classical analytic number theory]].<ref>{{cite book | title=Abstract Analytic Number Theory | first=John | last=Knopfmacher | edition=2nd | publisher=Dover Publishing | location=New York, NY | year=1990 | orig-year=1975 | isbn=0-486-66344-2 | zbl=0743.11002 }}</ref>}}
{{term|Abstract differential geometry}}
{{defn| A form of [[differential geometry]] without the notion of [[smoothness]] from [[calculus]]. Instead it is built using [[sheaf theory]] and [[sheaf cohomology]].}}
{{term|[[Abstract harmonic analysis]]}}
{{defn| A modern branch of [[harmonic analysis]] that extends upon the generalized [[Fourier transform]]s that can be defined on [[locally compact group]]s.}}
{{term|[[homotopy theory|Abstract homotopy theory]]}}
{{defn| A part of [[topology]] that deals with homotopic functions, i.e. functions from one topological space to another which are homotopic (the functions can be deformed into one another).}}
{{term|[[Actuarial science]]}}
{{defn| The discipline that applies [[mathematics|mathematical]] and [[statistics|statistical]] methods to [[Risk assessment|assess risk]] in [[insurance]], [[finance]] and other industries and professions. More generally, actuaries apply rigorous mathematics to model matters of uncertainty.}}
{{term|[[Additive combinatorics]]}}
{{defn| The part of [[arithmetic combinatorics]] devoted to the operations of [[addition]] and [[subtraction]].}}
{{term|[[Additive number theory]]}}
{{defn| A part of [[number theory]] that studies subsets of [[integer]]s and their behaviour under addition.}}
{{term|[[Affine geometry]]}}
{{defn| A branch of [[geometry]] that deals with properties that are independent from distances and angles, such as [[collinearity|alignment]] and [[parallel (geometry)|parallelism]].}}
{{term|[[Affine geometry of curves]]}}
{{defn| The study of [[curve]] properties that are invariant under [[affine transformation]]s.}}
{{term|[[Affine differential geometry]]}}
{{defn| A type of [[differential geometry]] dedicated to differential [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]]s under [[volume]]-preserving [[affine transformation]]s.}}
{{term|[[Ahlfors theory]]}}
{{defn| A part of [[complex analysis]] being the geometric counterpart of [[Nevanlinna theory]]. It was invented by [[Lars Ahlfors]].}}
{{term|[[Algebra]]}}
{{defn| One of the major [[areas of mathematics]]. Roughly speaking, it is the art of manipulating and computing with [[operation (mathematics)|operation]]s acting on symbols called [[variable (mathematics)|variable]]s that represent indeterminate [[number]]s or other [[mathematical object]]s, such as [[vector (mathematics and physics)|vector]]s, [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]], or elements of [[algebraic structure]]s.}}
{{term|[[Algebraic analysis]]}}
{{defn| motivated by systems of [[Linear differential equation|linear]] [[partial differential equation]]s, it is a branch of [[algebraic geometry]] and [[algebraic topology]] that uses methods from [[sheaf theory]] and complex analysis, to study the properties and generalizations of [[function (mathematics)|function]]s. It was started by [[Mikio Sato]].}}
{{term|[[Algebraic combinatorics]]}}
{{defn| an area that employs methods of abstract algebra to problems of [[combinatorics]]. It also refers to the application of methods from combinatorics to problems in abstract algebra.}}
{{term|[[Algebraic computation]]}}
{{defn| An older name of [[computer algebra]].}}
{{term|[[Algebraic geometry]]}}
{{defn| a branch that combines techniques from abstract algebra with the language and problems of geometry. Fundamentally, it studies [[algebraic varieties]].}}
{{term|[[Algebraic graph theory]]}}
{{defn| a branch of [[graph theory]] in which methods are taken from algebra and employed to problems about [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]]s. The methods are commonly taken from [[group theory]] and linear algebra.}}
{{term| [[Algebraic K-theory]]}}
{{defn| an important part of [[homological algebra]] concerned with defining and applying a certain sequence of [[functor]]s from [[ring (mathematics)|ring]]s to [[abelian group]]s.}}
{{term| [[Algebraic number theory]]}}
{{defn| The part of {{gli|number theory}} devoted to the use of algebraic methods, mainly those of {{gli|commutative algebra}}, for the study of [[number field]]s and their [[rings of integers]].}}
{{term|[[Algebraic statistics]]}}
{{defn| the use of algebra to advance [[statistics]], although the term is sometimes restricted to label the use of algebraic geometry and [[commutative algebra]] in [[statistics]].}}
{{term|[[Algebraic topology]]}}
{{defn |a branch that uses tools from [[abstract algebra]] for [[topology]] to study [[topological space]]s.}}
{{term|[[Algorithmic number theory]]}}
{{defn| also known as ''computational number theory'', it is the study of [[algorithm]]s for performing [[number theory|number theoretic]] [[computation]]s.}}
{{term|[[Anabelian geometry]]}}
{{defn| an area of study based on the theory proposed by [[Alexander Grothendieck]] in the 1980s that describes the way a geometric object of an [[algebraic variety]] (such as an [[algebraic fundamental group]]) can be mapped into another object, without it being an [[abelian group]].}}
{{term|[[Mathematical analysis|Analysis]]}}
{{defn | A wide area of mathematics centered on the study of [[continuous function]]s and including such topics as [[differentiation (mathematics)|differentiation]], [[integration (mathematics)|integration]], [[limit (mathematics)|limit]]s, and [[series (mathematics)|series]].<ref>{{cite book| first=Tom M. | last=Apostol | author-link= Tom M. Apostol | title=Mathematical Analysis: A Modern Approach to Advanced Calculus| edition= 2 |publisher=Addison-Wesley  }}</ref>}}
{{term |[[Analytic combinatorics]]}}
{{defn| part of [[enumerative combinatorics]] where methods of complex analysis are applied to [[generating function]]s.}}
{{term |[[Analytic geometry]]}}
{{defn|no=1|Also known as {{gli|Cartesian geometry}}, the study of {{gli|Euclidean geometry}} using  [[Cartesian coordinates]].}}
{{defn|no=2|Analogue to {{gli|differential geometry}}, where [[differentiable function]]s are replaced with [[analytic function]]s. It is a subarea of both {{gli|complex analysis}} and {{gli|algebraic geometry}}.}}
{{term| [[Analytic number theory]]}}
{{defn | An area of [[number theory]] that applies methods from [[mathematical analysis]] to solve problems about [[integer]]s.<ref>{{Apostol IANT}}</ref>}}
{{term| [[L-function|Analytic theory of L-function]]s}}
{{term |[[Applied mathematics]]}}
{{defn | a combination of various parts of mathematics that concern a variety of mathematical methods that can be applied to practical and theoretical problems. Typically the methods used are for [[science]], [[engineering]], [[finance]], [[economics]] and [[logistics]].}}
{{term|[[Approximation theory]]}}
{{defn| part of [[analysis]] that studies how well functions can be approximated by simpler ones (such as [[polynomial]]s or [[trigonometric polynomial]]s)}}
{{term|[[Arakelov geometry]]}}
{{defn| also known as ''Arakelov theory''}}
{{term| [[Arakelov theory]]}}
{{defn| an approach to [[Diophantine geometry]] used to study [[Diophantine equation]]s in higher dimensions (using techniques from algebraic geometry). It is named after [[Suren Arakelov]].}}
{{term| [[Arithmetic]]}}
{{defn|no=1| Also known as {{gli|elementary arithmetic}}, the methods and rules for computing with [[addition]], [[subtraction]], [[multiplication]] and [[division (mathematics)|division]] of numbers.}}
{{defn|no=2| Also known as {{gli|higher arithmetic}}, another name for [[number theory]].}}
{{term| [[Arithmetic algebraic geometry]]}}
{{defn| See {{gli|arithmetic geometry}}.}}
{{term|[[Arithmetic combinatorics]]}}
{{defn| the study of the estimates from [[combinatorics]] that are associated with [[arithmetic operation]]s such as addition, [[subtraction]], [[multiplication]] and [[division (mathematics)|division]].}}
{{term |[[Arithmetic dynamics]]}}
{{defn| Arithmetic dynamics is the study of the number-theoretic properties of [[integer point|integer]], [[rational point|rational]], {{mvar|p}}-adic, and/or algebraic points under repeated application of a [[polynomial]] or [[rational function]]. A fundamental goal is to describe arithmetic properties in terms of underlying geometric structures.}}
{{term| [[Arithmetic geometry]]}}
{{defn| The use of [[algebraic geometry]] and more specially [[scheme theory]] for solving problems of number theory.}}
{{term| [[Arithmetic topology]]}}
{{defn | a combination of [[algebraic number theory]] and [[topology]] studying analogies between [[prime ideal]]s and [[knot (mathematics)|knot]]s}}
{{term| [[Arithmetical algebraic geometry]]}}
{{defn| Another name for {{gli|arithmetic algebraic geometry}}}}
{{term| [[Asymptotic combinatorics]]}}
{{defn| It uses the internal structure of the objects to derive formulas for their [[generating function]]s and then complex analysis techniques to get asymptotics.}}
{{term| [[Asymptotic theory]]}} 
{{defn| the study of [[asymptotic expansion]]s}}
{{term| [[Auslander–Reiten theory]]}}
{{defn| the study of the [[representation theory]] of [[Artinian ring]]s}}
{{term| Axiomatic geometry}}
{{defn| also known as ''[[synthetic geometry]]'': it is a branch of geometry that uses [[axiom]]s and [[logical argument]]s to draw conclusions as opposed to [[analytic geometry|analytic]] and algebraic methods.}}
{{term| [[Axiomatic set theory]]}}
{{defn| the study of systems of [[axiom]]s in a context relevant to [[set theory]] and [[mathematical logic]].}}
{{glossary end}}

==B==

{{glossary}}
{{term| [[Bifurcation theory]]}}
{{defn| the study of changes in the qualitative or topological structure of a given family. It is a part of [[dynamical systems theory]]}}
{{term| [[Biostatistics]]}}
{{defn | the development and application of [[statistical]] methods to a wide range of topics in [[biology]].}}
{{term| [[Birational geometry]]}}
{{defn |a part of [[algebraic geometry]] that deals with the geometry (of an algebraic variety) that is dependent only on its [[function field of an algebraic variety|function field]].}}
{{term| Bolyai–Lobachevskian geometry}}
{{defn| see ''{{gli|hyperbolic geometry}}''}}
{{glossary end}}

==C==

{{glossary}}
{{term| [[C*-algebra|C*-algebra theory]]}}
{{defn | a [[complex number|complex]] [[algebra over a field|algebra]] ''A'' of [[continuous linear operator]]s on a [[complex number|complex]] [[Hilbert space]] with two additional properties-(i) ''A'' is a topologically [[closed set]] in the [[norm topology]] of operators.(ii)''A'' is closed under the operation of taking [[adjoint of an operator|adjoint]]s of operators.}}
{{term | [[Cartesian geometry]]}}
{{defn | see ''analytic geometry''}}
{{term | [[Calculus]]}}
{{defn | An area of mathematics connected by the [[fundamental theorem of calculus]].<ref>{{cite book |first1=Henry F. |last1=DeBaggis |first2=Kenneth S. |last2=Miller |title=Foundations of the Calculus |location=Philadelphia |publisher=Saunders |year=1966 |oclc=527896 }}</ref>}}
{{term | [[Infinitesimal calculus|Calculus of infinitesimal]]s}}
{{ghat|Also called '''infinitesimal calculus'''}}
{{defn | A foundation of [[calculus]], first developed in the 17th century,<ref>{{cite book |first=Carl B. |last=Boyer |author-link=Carl Benjamin Boyer |title=The History of the Calculus and its Conceptual Development |url=https://archive.org/details/historyofcalculu0000boye |url-access=registration |location=New York |publisher=Dover |year=1959 |oclc=643872 }}</ref> that makes use of [[infinitesimal]] numbers.}}
{{term | [[Calculus of moving surfaces]]}}
{{defn| an extension of the theory of [[tensor|tensor calculus]] to include deforming [[manifold]]s.}}
{{term | [[Calculus of variation]]s}}
{{defn | the field dedicated to maximizing or minimizing [[functional (mathematics)|functional]]s. It used to be called ''functional calculus''.}}
{{term | [[Catastrophe theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[bifurcation theory]] from [[dynamical systems theory]], and also a special case of the more general [[singularity theory]] from geometry. It analyses the [[germ (mathematics)|germ]]s of the catastrophe geometries.}}
{{term| [[Categorical logic]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[category theory]] adjacent to the [[mathematical logic]]. It is based on [[type theory]] for [[intuitionistic logic]]s.}}
{{term| [[Category theory]]}}
{{defn | the study of the properties of particular mathematical concepts by formalising them as collections of objects and arrows.}}
{{term | [[Chaos theory]]}}
{{defn | the study of the behaviour of [[dynamical system]]s that are highly sensitive to their initial conditions.}}
{{term | [[Character theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[group theory]] that studies the characters of [[group representation]]s or [[modular representation theory|modular representation]]s.}}
{{term | [[Class field theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[algebraic number theory]] that studies [[abelian extension]]s of [[number field]]s.}}
{{term | [[Differential geometry|Classical differential geometry]]}}
{{defn | also known as [[differential geometry|Euclidean differential geometry]]. see ''Euclidean differential geometry''.}}
{{term | [[Algebraic topology|Classical algebraic topology]]}}
{{defn | see ''algebraic topology''}}
{{term | [[Classical analysis]]}}
{{defn | usually refers to the more traditional topics of analysis such as [[real analysis]] and complex analysis. It includes any work that does not use techniques from [[functional analysis]] and is sometimes called ''hard analysis''. However it may also refer to mathematical analysis done according to the principles of [[classical mathematics]].}}
{{term | [[Analytic number theory|Classical analytic number theory]]}}
{{term  | [[Differential calculus|Classical differential calculus]]}}
{{term | [[Diophantine geometry|Classical Diophantine geometry]]}}
{{term | [[Euclidean geometry|Classical Euclidean geometry]]}} 
{{ defn | see ''Euclidean geometry''}}
{{ term | Classical geometry}}
{{defn | may refer to [[solid geometry]] or classical Euclidean geometry. See ''geometry''}}
{{term | [[Invariant theory|Classical invariant theory]]}}
{{defn | the form of [[invariant theory]] that deals with describing [[polynomial function]]s that are [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] under transformations from a given [[linear group]].}}
{{term | [[Classical mathematics]]}}
{{defn | the standard approach to mathematics based on [[classical logic]] and [[ZFC set theory]].}}
{{term | [[Projective geometry|Classical projective geometry]]}}
{{term | [[tensor|Classical tensor calculus]]}}
{{term | [[Clifford algebra]]}}
{{term | [[Clifford analysis]]}}
{{defn|the study of [[Dirac operator]]s and [[Dirac operator|Dirac type operator]]s from geometry and analysis using [[clifford algebra]]s.}}
{{term | [[Clifford theory]]}}
{{defn | is a branch of [[representation theory]] spawned from [[Clifford theory|Cliffords theorem]].}}
{{term | [[Cobordism theory]]}}
{{term | [[Coding theory]]}}
{{defn | the study of the properties of [[code]]s and their respective fitness for specific applications.}}
{{term | [[Cohomology theory]]}}
{{term| [[Combinatorial analysis]]}}
{{term | [[Combinatorial commutative algebra]]}}
{{defn | a discipline viewed as the intersection between [[commutative algebra]] and combinatorics. It frequently employs methods from one to address problems arising in the other. [[Polyhedral geometry]] also plays a significant role.}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial design theory]]}}
{{defn | a part of combinatorial mathematics that deals with the existence and construction of [[Set system|systems of finite set]]s whose intersections have certain properties.}}
{{term | [[Combinatorial game theory]]}}
{{term | [[Combinatorial geometry]]}}
{{defn | see ''discrete geometry''}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial group theory]]}}
{{defn | the theory of [[free group]]s and the [[presentation of a group]]. It is closely related to [[geometric group theory]] and is applied in [[geometric topology]].}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial mathematics]]}}
{{defn| an area primarily concerned with counting, both as a means and an end in obtaining results, and certain properties of [[finite set|finite]] [[Mathematical structure|structure]]s.}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial number theory]]}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial optimization]]}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial set theory]]}}
{{defn | also known as [[Infinitary combinatorics]]. see ''infinitary combinatorics''}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial theory]]}}
{{term |[[Combinatorial topology]]}}
{{defn | an old name for algebraic topology, when [[topological invariant]]s of spaces were regarded as derived from combinatorial decompositions.}}
{{term |[[Combinatorics]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[discrete mathematics]] concerned with [[countable set|countable]] [[mathematical structure|structure]]s. Branches of it include [[enumerative combinatorics]], [[combinatorial design theory]], [[matroid theory]], [[extremal combinatorics]] and [[algebraic combinatorics]], as well as many more.}}
{{term |[[Commutative algebra]]}}
{{defn | a branch of abstract algebra studying [[commutative ring]]s.}}
{{term |[[Complex algebraic geometry]]}}
{{defn | the mainstream of algebraic geometry devoted to the study of the [[complex number|complex]] points of [[algebraic varieties]].}}
{{term |[[Complex analysis]]}}
{{defn | a part of [[analysis]] that deals with functions of a [[complex numbers|complex]] variable.}}
{{term |[[Complex analytic dynamics]]}}
{{defn | a subdivision of [[complex dynamics]] being the study of the [[dynamic system]]s defined by [[analytic function]]s.}}
{{term |[[Complex analytic geometry]]}}
{{defn | the application of complex numbers to [[plane geometry]].}}
{{term |[[Differential geometry|Complex differential geometry]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[differential geometry]] that studies [[complex manifold]]s.}}
{{term |[[Complex dynamics]]}}
{{defn | the study of [[dynamical system]]s defined by [[iterated function]]s on complex [[number space]]s.}}
{{term |[[Complex geometry]]}} 
{{defn | the study of [[complex manifold]]s and functions of [[complex numbers|complex]] variables. It includes [[complex algebraic geometry]] and [[complex analytic geometry]].}}
{{term |[[Complexity theory (disambiguation)|Complexity theory]]}}
{{defn | the study of [[complex system]]s with the inclusion of the theory of [[complex system]]s.}}
{{term |[[Computable analysis]]}}
{{defn | the study of which parts of [[real analysis]] and [[functional analysis]] can be carried out in a [[computability theory|computable]] manner. It is closely related to [[constructive analysis]].}}
{{term |[[Computable model theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[model theory]] dealing with the relevant questions [[computability]].}}
{{term |[[Computability theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[mathematical logic]] originating in the 1930s with the study of [[computable function]]s and [[Turing degree]]s, but now includes the study of generalized computability and definability. It overlaps with [[proof theory]] and [[effective descriptive set theory]].}}
{{term |[[Computational algebraic geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Computational complexity theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of mathematics and [[theoretical computer science]] that focuses on classifying [[computational problem]]s according to their inherent difficulty, and relating those [[complexity class|classes]] to each other.}}
{{term |[[Computational geometry]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[computer science]] devoted to the study of algorithms which can be stated in terms of [[geometry]].}} 
{{term |[[Computational group theory]]}}
{{defn | the study of [[group (mathematics)|group]]s by means of computers.}}
{{term |[[Computational mathematics]]}}
{{defn | the mathematical research in areas of [[science]] where [[computation|computing]] plays an essential role.}}
{{term |[[Computational number theory]]}}
{{defn | also known as ''algorithmic number theory'', it is the study of [[algorithm]]s for performing [[number theory|number theoretic]] [[computation]]s.}}
{{term |[[Computational statistics]]}}
{{term |[[Computational synthetic geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Computational topology]]}}
{{term |[[Computer algebra]]}}
{{defn | see ''symbolic computation''}}
{{term |[[Conformal geometry]]}}
{{defn | the study of [[conformal map|conformal]] transformations on a space.}}
{{term |[[Constructive analysis]]}}
{{defn | mathematical analysis done according to the principles of [[constructive mathematics]]. This differs from ''classical analysis''.}}
{{term |[[Constructive function theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of analysis that is closely related to [[approximation theory]], studying the connection between the [[smooth function|smoothness of a function]] and its [[approximation theory|degree of approximation]]}}
{{term |[[Constructive mathematics]]}}
{{defn | mathematics which tends to use [[intuitionistic logic]]. Essentially that is classical logic but without the assumption that the [[law of the excluded middle]] is an [[axiom]].}}
{{term |[[Constructive quantum field theory]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[mathematical physics]] that is devoted to showing that [[quantum mechanics|quantum theory]] is mathematically compatible with [[special relativity]].}}
{{term |[[Constructive set theory]]}}
{{defn | an approach to [[constructivism (mathematics)|mathematical constructivism]] following the program of [[axiomatic set theory]], using the usual [[first-order logic|first-order]] language of classical set theory.}}
{{term |[[Contact geometry]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[differential geometry]] and [[differential topology|topology]], closely related to and considered the odd-dimensional counterpart of [[symplectic geometry]]. It is the study of a geometric structure called a contact structure on a [[differentiable manifold]].}}
{{term |[[Convex analysis]]}}
{{defn | the study of properties of [[convex function]]s and [[convex set]]s.}}
{{term |[[Convex geometry]]}}
{{defn | part of geometry devoted to the study of [[convex set]]s.}}
{{term |[[Coordinate geometry]]}}
{{defn | see ''analytic geometry''}}
{{term |[[CR geometry]]}}
{{defn | a branch of [[differential geometry]], being the study of [[CR manifold]]s.}}
{{term |[[Cryptography]]}}
{{glossary end}}

==D==
 
{{glossary}}
{{term |[[Decision analysis]]}}
{{term |[[Decision theory]]}}
{{term |[[Noncommutative algebraic geometry|Derived noncommutative algebraic geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Descriptive set theory]]}}
{{defn |a part of [[mathematical logic]], more specifically a part of [[set theory]] dedicated to the study of [[Polish space]]s.}}
{{term |[[Differential algebraic geometry]]}}
{{defn |the adaption of methods and concepts from algebraic geometry to systems of [[algebraic differential equation]]s.}}
{{term |[[Differential calculus]]}}
{{defn |The branch of [[calculus]] contrasted to [[integral calculus]],<ref>{{Citation| first = R.| last = Courant| translator-first = E. J.| translator-last = McShane| title = Differential and Integral Calculus| volume = I| year= 1937| edition = 2nd| publisher = Interscience| place = New York}} {{isbn|978-4-87187-838-8}}</ref> and concerned with [[derivative]]s.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Definition of DIFFERENTIAL CALCULUS|url=https://merriam-webster.com/dictionary/differential+calculus|website=www.merriam-webster.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-09}}</ref>}}
{{term |[[Differential Galois theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of the [[Galois group]]s of [[differential field]]s.}}
{{term |[[Differential geometry]]}}
{{defn |a form of geometry that uses techniques from [[integral calculus|integral]] and [[differential calculus]] as well as [[linear algebra|linear]] and [[multilinear algebra]] to study problems in geometry. Classically, these were problems of Euclidean geometry, although now it has been expanded. It is generally concerned with geometric structures on [[differentiable manifold]]s. It is closely related to differential topology.}}
{{term |[[Differential geometry of curves]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[curve|smooth curve]]s in [[Euclidean space]] by using techniques from [[differential geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Differential geometry of surfaces]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[smooth manifold|smooth]] [[Surface (topology)|surface]]s with various additional structures using the techniques of [[differential geometry]].}}
{{term |[[Differential topology]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[topology]] that deals with [[differentiable function]]s on [[differentiable manifold]]s.}}
{{term |[[Diffiety|Diffiety theory]]}}
{{term |[[Diophantine geometry]]}}
{{defn |in general the study of algebraic varieties over [[field (mathematics)|field]]s that are finitely generated over their [[prime field]]s.}}
{{term |[[Discrepancy theory]]}}
{{term |[[Discrete differential geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Discrete exterior calculus]]}}
{{term |[[Discrete geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[geometry]] that studies [[Combinatorics|combinatorial]] properties and constructive methods of [[discrete mathematics|discrete]] geometric objects.}}
{{term |[[Discrete mathematics]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[mathematical structure]]s that are fundamentally [[discrete space|discrete]] rather than [[continuous function|continuous]].}}
{{term |[[Discrete Morse theory]]}}
{{defn |a [[combinatorial]] adaption of [[Morse theory]].}}
{{term |[[Distance geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Domain theory]]}}
{{defn |a branch that studies special kinds of [[partially ordered set]]s (posets) commonly called domains.}}
{{term |[[Donaldson theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of smooth [[4-manifold]]s using [[gauge theory]].}}
{{term |[[Dyadics|Dyadic algebra]]}}
{{term |[[Dynamical systems theory]]}}
{{defn |an area used to describe the behavior of the [[complex systems|complex]] [[dynamical system]]s, usually by employing [[differential equation]]s or [[difference equation]]s.}}
{{glossary end}}

==E==

{{glossary}}
{{term |[[Econometrics]]}}
{{defn |the application of mathematical and [[statistics|statistical]] methods to [[Economics|economic]] [[data]].}}
{{term |[[Effective descriptive set theory]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[descriptive set theory]] dealing with [[set (mathematics)|set]] of [[real number]]s that have [[lightface]] definitions. It uses aspects of [[computability theory]].}}
{{term |[[Elementary algebra]]}}
{{defn |a fundamental form of [[algebra]] extending on [[elementary arithmetic]] to include the concept of [[variable (mathematics)|variable]]s.}}
{{term |[[Elementary arithmetic]]}}
{{defn |the simplified portion of arithmetic considered necessary for [[primary education]]. It includes the usage addition, [[subtraction]], [[multiplication]] and [[division (mathematics)|division]] of the [[natural number]]s. It also includes the concept of [[fraction (mathematics)|fraction]]s and [[negative number]]s.}}
{{term |[[Elementary mathematics]]}}
{{defn |parts of mathematics frequently taught at the [[primary school|primary]] and [[secondary school]] levels. This includes [[elementary arithmetic]], geometry, [[probability]] and [[statistics]], [[elementary algebra]] and [[trigonometry]]. (calculus is not usually considered a part)}}
{{term |[[Elementary group theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of the basics of [[group theory]]}}
{{term |[[Elimination theory]]}}
{{defn |the classical name for algorithmic approaches to eliminating between [[polynomial]]s of several variables. It is a part of [[commutative algebra]] and algebraic geometry.}}
{{term |[[Elliptic geometry]]}}
{{defn |a type of [[non-Euclidean geometry]] (it violates [[Euclid]]'s [[parallel postulate]]) and is based on [[spherical geometry]]. It is constructed in [[elliptic space]].}}
{{term |[[Enumerative combinatorics]]}}
{{defn |an area of combinatorics that deals with the number of ways that certain patterns can be formed.}}
{{term |[[Enumerative geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of algebraic geometry concerned with counting the number of solutions to geometric questions. This is usually done by means of [[intersection theory]].}}
{{term |[[Epidemiology]]}}
{{term |[[Noncommutative algebraic geometry|Equivariant noncommutative algebraic geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Ergodic Ramsey theory]]}}
{{defn |a branch where problems are motivated by [[additive combinatorics]] and solved using [[ergodic theory]].}}
{{term |[[Ergodic theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[dynamical system]]s with an [[invariant measure]], and related problems.}}
{{term |[[Euclidean geometry]]}}
{{defn | An area of [[geometry]] based on the [[axiom system]] and [[synthetic geometry|synthetic method]]s of the ancient Greek mathematician [[Euclid]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Howard|last= Eves|title=A Survey of Geometry (Volume One)|publisher=Allyn and Bacon|year=1963}}</ref>}}
{{term |[[Differential geometry|Euclidean differential geometry]]}}
{{defn |also known as ''classical differential geometry''. See ''differential geometry''.}}
{{term |[[Euler calculus]]}}
{{defn |a methodology from applied [[algebraic topology]] and [[integral geometry]] that integrates [[constructible function]]s and more recently [[definable function]]s by integrating with respect to the [[Euler characteristic]] as a finitely-additive [[measure theory|measure]].}}
{{term |[[Experimental mathematics]]}}
{{defn |an approach to mathematics in which computation is used to investigate mathematical objects and identify properties and patterns.}}
{{term | Exterior algebra}}
{{term | Exterior calculus}}
{{term |[[Extraordinary cohomology theory]]}}
{{term |[[Extremal combinatorics]]}}
{{defn |a branch of combinatorics, it is the study of the possible sizes of a collection of finite objects given certain restrictions.}}
{{term |[[Extremal graph theory]]}}
{{defn |a branch of mathematics that studies how global properties of a graph influence local substructure.}}
{{glossary end}}

{{term |[[Finite geometry]]}}

{{term |[[Fractal geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Fractional calculus]]}}
{{defn |a branch of analysis that studies the possibility of taking [[real number|real]] or complex powers of the [[differentiation operator]].}}
{{term |[[Fractional dynamics]]}}
{{defn |investigates the behaviour of objects and systems that are described by [[Derivative|differentiation]] and [[integral|integration]] of [[fraction (mathematics)|fractional]] orders using methods of [[fractional calculus]].}}
{{term |[[Fredholm theory]]}}
{{defn |part of [[spectral theory]] studying [[integral equation]]s.}}
{{term |[[Function theory (disambiguation)|Function theory]]}}
{{defn |an ambiguous term that generally refers to [[mathematical analysis]].}}

{{term |[[Functional calculus]]}}
{{defn |historically the term was used synonymously with [[calculus of variations]], but now refers to a branch of [[functional analysis]] connected with [[spectral theory]]}}
{{term |[[Fuzzy mathematics]]}}
{{defn |a branch of mathematics based on [[fuzzy set theory]] and [[fuzzy logic]].}}
{{term |[[Fuzzy measure theory]]}}
{{term |[[Fuzzy set theory]]}}

==G==

{{glossary}}
{{term |[[Galois cohomology]]}}
{{defn |an application of [[homological algebra]], it is the study of [[group cohomology]] of [[Galois module]]s.}}
{{term |[[Galois theory]]}}
{{defn |named after [[Évariste Galois]], it is a branch of abstract algebra providing a connection between [[field theory (mathematics)|field theory]] and [[group theory]].}}
{{term |[[Galois geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[finite geometry]] concerned with algebraic and [[analytic geometry|analytic]] geometry over a [[Galois field]].}}
{{term |[[Game theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[mathematical model]]s of strategic interaction among rational decision-makers.}}
{{term |[[Gauge theory]]}}
{{term |[[General topology]]}}
{{defn |also known as ''point-set topology'', it is a branch of [[topology]] studying the properties of [[topological space]]s and structures defined on them. It differs from other branches of [[topology]] as the [[topological space]]s do not have to be similar to manifolds.}}
{{term |[[Generalized trigonometry]]}}
{{defn |developments of [[trigonometry|trigonometric]] methods from the application to [[real number]]s of Euclidean geometry to any geometry or [[space]]. This includes [[spherical trigonometry]], [[hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic trigonometry]], [[gyrotrigonometry]], and [[rational trigonometry|universal hyperbolic trigonometry]].}}
{{term |[[Geometric algebra]]}}
{{defn |an alternative approach to classical, [[computational geometry|computational]] and [[Special relativity|relativistic geometry]]. It shows a natural correspondence between geometric entities and elements of algebra.}}
{{term |[[Geometric analysis]]}}
{{defn |a discipline that uses methods from [[differential geometry]] to study [[partial differential equation]]s as well as the applications to geometry.}}
{{term |[[Geometric calculus]]}}
{{defn |extends the [[geometric algebra]] to include [[Derivative|differentiation]] and [[Integral|integration]].}}
{{term |[[Geometric combinatorics]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[combinatorics]].  It includes a number of subareas such as [[polyhedral combinatorics]] (the study of [[Face (geometry)|face]]s of [[convex polyhedron|convex polyhedra]]), [[convex geometry]] (the study of [[convex set]]s, in particular combinatorics of their intersections), and [[discrete geometry]], which in turn has many applications to [[computational geometry]].}}
{{term |[[Geometric function theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of geometric properties of [[analytic function]]s.}}
{{term |[[Geometric invariant theory]]}}
{{defn |a method for constructing quotients by [[Group action (mathematics)|group action]]s in [[algebraic geometry]], used to construct [[moduli space]]s.}}
{{term |[[Geometric graph theory]]}}
{{defn |a large and amorphous subfield of [[graph theory]], concerned with graphs defined by geometric means.}}
{{term |[[Geometric group theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[finitely generated group]]s via exploring the connections between algebraic properties of such groups and [[topology|topological]] and [[geometry|geometric]] properties of spaces on which these groups [[Group action (mathematics)|act]] (that is, when the groups in question are realized as geometric symmetries or continuous transformations of some spaces).}}
{{term |[[Geometric measure theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[geometry|geometric]] properties of [[Set (mathematics)|set]]s (typically in [[Euclidean space]]) through [[measure (mathematics)|measure theory]].}}
{{term |[[Geometric number theory]]}}
{{term |[[Geometric topology]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[topology]] studying manifolds and mappings between them; in particular the [[embedding]] of one manifold into another.}}
{{term |[[Geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of mathematics concerned with [[shape]] and the properties of [[space (mathematics)|space]]. Classically it arose as what is now known as [[solid geometry]]; this was concerning practical knowledge of [[length]], [[area]] and [[volume]]. It was then put into an [[axiomatic system|axiomatic form]] by [[Euclid]], giving rise to what is now known as classical Euclidean geometry. The use of [[coordinate]]s by [[René Descartes]] gave rise to [[Cartesian geometry]] enabling a more analytical approach to geometric entities. Since then many other branches have appeared including [[projective geometry]], [[differential geometry]], [[non-Euclidean geometry]], [[Fractal geometry]] and algebraic geometry. Geometry also gave rise to the modern discipline of [[topology]].}}
{{term |[[Geometry of number]]s}}
{{defn |initiated by [[Hermann Minkowski]], it is a branch of [[number theory]] studying [[convex bodies]] and [[integer]] [[Euclidean vector|vector]]s.}}
{{term |[[Global analysis]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[differential equation]]s on manifolds and the relationship between [[differential equation]]s and [[topology]].}}
{{term |[[Arithmetic dynamics|Global arithmetic dynamics]]}}
{{term |[[Graph theory]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[discrete mathematics]] devoted to the study of [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]]s. It has many applications in [[physical science|physical]], [[biological science|biological]] and [[social science|social]] systems.}}
{{term |[[Character theory|Group-character theory]]}}
{{defn |the part of character theory dedicated to the study of characters of [[group representation]]s.}}
{{term |[[Group representation theory]]}}
{{term |[[Group theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[algebraic structure]]s known as [[group (mathematics)|group]]s.}}
{{term |[[Gyrotrigonometry]]}}
{{defn |a form of [[trigonometry]] used in [[gyrovector space]] for [[hyperbolic geometry]]. (An analogy of the [[vector space]] in Euclidean geometry.)}}
{{glossary end}}

==K==
{{glossary}}
{{term |[[K-theory]]}}
{{defn |originated as the study of a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]] generated by [[vector bundle]]s over a [[topological space]] or [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]. In algebraic topology it is an [[extraordinary cohomology theory]] known as [[topological K-theory]]. In algebra and algebraic geometry it is referred to as [[algebraic K-theory]]. In [[mathematical physics|physics]], [[K-theory (physics)|K-theory]] has appeared in [[type II string theory]]. (In particular [[twisted K-theory]].)}}
{{term |[[K-homology]]}}
{{defn |a [[homology (mathematics)|homology]] theory on the [[Category (mathematics)|category]] of locally [[compact space|compact]] [[Hausdorff space]]s. }}
{{term |[[Kähler manifold|Kähler geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[differential geometry]], more specifically a union of [[Riemannian geometry]], [[differential geometry|complex differential geometry]] and [[symplectic geometry]]. It is the study of [[Kähler manifold]]s. (named after [[Erich Kähler]])}}
{{term |[[KK-theory]]}}
{{defn |a common generalization both of [[K-homology]] and [[operator K-theory|K-theory]] as an additive [[functor#Bifunctors|bivariant functor]] on [[separable space|separable]] [[C*-algebra]]s.}}
{{term |[[Klein geometry]]}}
{{defn |More specifically, it is a [[homogeneous space]] ''X'' together with a [[Group action (mathematics)|transitive action]] on ''X'' by a [[Lie group]] ''G'', which acts as the [[symmetry group]] of the geometry.}}
{{term |[[Knot theory]]}}
{{defn |part of [[topology]] dealing with [[knot (mathematics)|knot]]s}}
{{term |[[Kummer theory]]}}
{{defn |provides a description of certain types of [[field extension]]s involving the [[adjunction (field theory)|adjunction]] of ''n''th roots of elements of the base [[field (mathematics)|field]]}}
{{glossary end}}

==R==

{{term|[[Ramsey theory]]}}
{{defn|the study of the conditions in which order must appear. It is named after [[Frank P. Ramsey]].}}

{{defn|the study of the part of algebra relevant to [[real algebraic geometry]].}}

{{defn|the part of algebraic geometry that studies [[real number|real]] points of the algebraic varieties.}}
{{term|[[Real analysis]]}}
{{defn|a branch of mathematical analysis; in particular ''hard analysis'', that is the study of [[real number]]s and [[function (mathematics)|function]]s of [[real number|Real]] values. It provides a rigorous formulation of the calculus of [[real number]]s in terms of [[continuous function|continuity]] and [[smooth function|smoothness]], whilst the theory is extended to the [[complex number]]s in [[complex analysis]].}}
{{term | Real Clifford algebra}}
{{term|[[Real K-theory]]}}

{{defn|the area dedicated to [[mathematical puzzle]]s and [[mathematical game]]s.}}
{{term|[[Recursion theory]]}}
{{defn|see ''computability theory''}}
{{term|[[Representation theory]]}}
{{defn|a subfield of abstract algebra; it studies [[algebraic structure]]s by representing their elements as [[linear transformation]]s of [[vector space]]s. It also studies [[module (mathematics)|module]]s over these algebraic structures, providing a way of reducing problems in abstract algebra to problems in linear algebra.}}
{{term|[[Group representation|Representation theory of group]]s}}
{{term|[[Representation theory of the Galilean group]]}}
{{term|[[Representation theory of the Lorentz group]]}}
{{term|[[Representation theory of the Poincaré group]]}}
{{term|[[Representation theory of the symmetric group]]}}
{{term|[[Ribbon theory]]}}
{{defn|a branch of [[topology]] studying [[ribbon (mathematics)|ribbon]]s.}}
{{term|[[Ricci calculus]]}}
{{defn| {{ghat|Also called '''absolute differential calculus'''.}}
A foundation of [[tensor calculus]], developed by [[Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro]] in 1887–1896,<ref>{{Citation |last1=Ricci |first1=Gregorio |author-link1=Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro |last2=Levi-Civita |first2=Tullio |author-link2=Tullio Levi-Civita |title=Méthodes de calcul différentiel absolu et leurs applications |trans-title=Methods of the absolute differential calculus and their applications |journal=[[Mathematische Annalen]] |date=March 1900 |access-date=19 October 2019 |volume=54 |issue=1–2 |pages=125–201 |doi=10.1007/BF01454201 |url=https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/resolveppn/?PPN=GDZPPN002258102 |publisher=Springer |s2cid=120009332 |language=fr}}</ref> and later developed for its applications to  [[general relativity]] and [[differential geometry]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Schouten|first=Jan A.|title=Der Ricci-Kalkül – Eine Einführung in die neueren Methoden und Probleme der mehrdimensionalen Differentialgeometrie (Ricci Calculus – An introduction in the latest methods and problems in multi-dimensional differential geometry)|language=de|year=1924|series=Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften|volume=10|editor= R. Courant|publisher=Springer Verlag|location=Berlin|url=https://resolver.sub.uni-goettingen.de/purl?PPN373339186}}</ref>}}
{{term|[[Ring theory]]}}
{{term|[[Riemannian geometry]]}}
{{defn|a branch of [[differential geometry]] that is more specifically, the study of [[Riemannian manifold]]s. It is named after [[Bernhard Riemann]] and it features many generalizations of concepts from Euclidean geometry, analysis and calculus.}}
{{term|[[Rough set|Rough set theory]]}}
{{defn|the a form of [[set theory]] based on [[rough set]]s.}}
{{glossary end}}

{{glossary}}
{{term |[[Sampling (statistics)|Sampling theory]]}}
{{term |[[Scheme (mathematics)|Scheme theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of [[scheme (mathematics)|scheme]]s introduced by [[Alexander Grothendieck]]. It allows the use of [[sheaf theory]] to study algebraic varieties and is considered the central part of ''modern algebraic geometry''.}}

{{defn |a part of algebraic geometry; more specifically a branch of [[real algebraic geometry]] that studies [[semialgebraic set]]s.}}

{{term |[[Set theory]]}}
{{term |[[Sheaf theory]]}}
{{defn| The study of [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheave]]s, which connect local and global properties of [[topological space|geometric object]]s.<ref>{{Citation | last1=Tennison | first1=Barry R. | title=Sheaf theory | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | mr=0404390  | year=1975 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JOglpKIw6kIC |isbn=978-0-521-20784-3 |volume=20 |series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series }}</ref>}}
{{term |[[Sheaf cohomology]]}}
{{term |[[Sieve theory]]}}
{{term |[[Operator theory|Single operator theory]]}}
{{defn |deals with the properties and classifications of single [[operator (mathematics)|operator]]s.}}
{{term |[[Singularity theory]]}}
{{defn |a branch, notably of geometry; that studies the failure of manifold structure.}}

{{defn |a rigorous reformation of [[infinitesimal calculus]] employing methods of [[category theory]]. As a theory, it is a subset of [[synthetic differential geometry]].}}
{{term |[[Solid geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Spatial geometry]]}}
{{term |[[Spectral geometry]]}}
{{defn |a field that concerns the relationships between geometric structures of manifolds and [[spectrum of an operator|spectra]] of canonically defined [[differential operator]]s.}}
{{term |[[Spectral graph theory]]}}
{{defn |the study of properties of a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] using methods from [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix theory]].}}

{{defn |part of ''operator theory'' extending the concepts of [[eigenvalue]]s and [[eigenvector]]s from linear algebra and [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix theory]].}}
{{term |[[Spectral theory of ordinary differential equations]]}}
{{defn |part of [[spectral theory]] concerned with the [[spectrum of an operator|spectrum]] and [[eigenfunction]] expansion associated with [[linear differential equation|linear]] [[ordinary differential equation]]s.}}
{{term |[[Spectrum continuation analysis]]}}
{{defn |generalizes the concept of a [[Fourier series]] to non-periodic [[function (mathematics)|function]]s.}}
{{term |[[Spherical geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[non-Euclidean geometry]], studying the 2-dimensional surface of a [[sphere]].}}
{{term |[[Spherical trigonometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[spherical geometry]] that studies [[polygon]]s on the surface of a [[sphere]]. Usually the [[polygon]]s are [[triangle]]s.}}
{{term |[[Statistical mechanics]]}}
{{term |[[Statistical modelling]]}}
{{term |[[Statistical theory]]}}
{{term |[[Mathematical statistics|Statistics]]}}
{{defn |although the term may refer to the more general study of [[statistics]], the term is used in mathematics to refer to the [[mathematical statistics|mathematical study of statistics and related field]]s. This includes [[probability theory]].}}
{{term |[[Steganography]]}}
{{term |[[Stochastic calculus]]}}
{{term |[[Malliavin calculus|Stochastic calculus of variation]]s}}
{{term |[[Stochastic geometry]]}}
{{defn |the study of random patterns of points}}
{{term |[[Stochastic process]]}}
{{term |[[Stratified Morse theory]]}}
{{term |[[Super linear algebra]]}}
{{term |[[Surgery theory]]}}
{{defn |a part of [[geometric topology]] referring to methods used to produce one manifold from another (in a controlled way.)}}
{{term |[[Survey sampling]]}}
{{term |[[Survey methodology]]}}
{{term |[[Symbolic computation]]}}
{{defn |also known as ''algebraic computation'' and ''computer algebra''. It refers to the techniques used to manipulate [[expression (mathematics)|mathematical expression]]s and [[equation]]s in [[symbol|symbolic form]] as opposed to manipulating them by the numerical quantities represented by them.}}
{{term |[[Symbolic dynamics]]}}
{{term |[[Symplectic geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[differential geometry]] and topology whose main object of study is the [[symplectic manifold]].}}
{{term |[[Symplectic topology]]}}
{{term |[[Synthetic differential geometry]]}}
{{defn |a reformulation of [[differential geometry]] in the language of [[topos theory]] and in the context of an [[intuitionistic logic]].}}

{{defn |also known as '''axiomatic geometry''', it is a branch of geometry that uses [[axiom]]s and [[logical argument]]s to draw conclusions as opposed to [[analytic geometry|analytic]] and algebraic methods.}}
{{term |[[Systolic geometry]]}}
{{defn |a branch of [[differential geometry]] studying systolic [[invariant (mathematics)|invariant]]s of [[manifold]]s and [[polyhedra]].}}
{{term |[[Systolic geometry|Systolic hyperbolic geometry]]}}
